quizName: DMV Practice Test #15 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: A motorcycle's brake light is _________ a car's brake light.
questions.correctAnswerText: Not as noticeable as
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is usually not as noticeable as a car's brake light, especially when the taillight is already on. Other drivers may not see your brake light.

questions.question: A solid white line on the side of the road means:

options.text: The right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of a traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the side of the road shows the right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks up while stopping on a road with good grip, you should:

options.text: Keep the wheel locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake and apply it again quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the wheel locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on a road with good grip, you can keep it locked until you stop. You can still control your motorcycle if it stays upright and goes straight.

questions.question: When riding in a group, inexperienced riders should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the lead rider.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride near the front, just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders watch them from behind.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Avoid using your high beam headlight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: When riding at night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance. Use your high beam headlight when there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Service signs are:
questions.correctAnswerText: Blue with white letters.
questions.explanation: Blue signs with white letters show where services are located. Services include rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: If you wear a jacket for protection while riding in hot weather, you should:

options.text: Take frequent breaks to cool off.
Remove the jacket to stay cool in the sun.
Keep the jacket on to protect you from heat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the jacket on to protect you from heat.
questions.explanation: A riding jacket provides protection in a crash, no matter the weather. In hot weather, jackets also protect you from dehydration. Many riding jackets are designed to prevent overheating.

questions.question: Before starting a turn, a rider should change gears to:

options.text: Prevent power changes in the middle of the turn.
Keep both hands on the handle grips during the turn.
Prevent the motorcycle from slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent power changes in the middle of the turn.
questions.explanation: Change gears before starting a turn. Shifting during a turn can cause a sudden power change to the rear wheel and cause a skid. If you must shift during a turn, do it smoothly to prevent skidding.

questions.question: Where is the gearshift located?

options.text: In front of the left footrest
In front of the right footrest

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest and you operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a factor in blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: How quickly the alcohol is consumed
How often the person drinks alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often the person drinks alcohol
questions.explanation: BAC is determined by body weight, how much alcohol is consumed, and how quickly it is consumed. Never ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: A sign that your front tire is flat is that steering suddenly feels:
questions.correctAnswerText: Heavy.
questions.explanation: If steering suddenly feels heavy, your front tire may be flat. Stop and check your tires right away.

questions.question: _________ of crashes between motorcycles and cars happen because the car driver did not yield the right-of-way to the motorcycle.
questions.correctAnswerText: More than half
questions.explanation: More than half of crashes between motorcycles and cars are caused by car drivers failing to yield to motorcyclists. Motorcyclists should never assume that car drivers will yield, even if they are required to do so.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Divided roadway ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns of a divided roadway ahead.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
The rear brake is more powerful than the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: Your normal scanning routine while riding should include:

options.text: Always looking in the rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Checking the rearview mirror often.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirror often as part of your normal scanning. Also check your mirrors before changing lanes, at intersections, and before slowing down.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:
questions.correctAnswerText: In broad daylight.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright colors and reflective materials when riding, even in daylight.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, a motorcyclist should not:

options.text: Choose a lane position that makes them more visible.
Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
Have the clutch and brakes ready to reduce reaction time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that other drivers can see you. Have the clutch and brakes ready to react quickly. Slow down as you approach the intersection. Avoid sudden speed or position changes that could confuse other drivers.

questions.question: Shifting gears while turning:

options.text: Should only be done if it can be done smoothly.
Is better than shifting before the turn.
Is the best way to control speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should only be done if it can be done smoothly.
questions.explanation: Shift gears before you start a turn. If you must shift while turning, do it smoothly. A sudden power change can make the rear wheel skid.

questions.question: While riding, you should wear:

options.text: Hearing protection to prevent damage from engine and wind noise.
A helmet to protect your hearing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hearing protection to prevent damage from engine and wind noise.
questions.explanation: Long-term exposure to engine and wind noise can damage your hearing, even with a full-face helmet. Use hearing protection to prevent damage.

questions.question: When preparing to ride with a passenger, instruct the passenger to:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle before you.
Sit as far back as possible.
Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.
questions.explanation: Have your passenger wait to get on after you start the engine. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding you and hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Stay within the posted speed limit.
Go up to 10 mph over the speed limit to complete the pass.
Pass more than one vehicle at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay within the posted speed limit.
questions.explanation: All passes must be done within the legal speed limit. Only pass where it is safe and legal.

questions.question: Your motorcycle starts to weave while riding over uneven metal bridge gratings. What should you do?

options.text: Shift to a lower gear right away.
Zigzag across the bridge until you reach the other side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax and steer straight.
questions.explanation: If your motorcycle weaves on uneven surfaces or bridge gratings, simply relax and go straight at a steady speed. Zigzagging is more dangerous than the weaving.

questions.question: When riding through a curve, where should you position your motorcycle?

options.text: Always in the right part of the lane.
Always in the left part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change position based on conditions.
questions.explanation: Every curve is different. Change your lane position as road, traffic, and weather conditions change.

questions.question: To turn safely on a motorcycle, you should always:

options.text: Lean in the direction of the turn.
Slow down while in the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: Always lean in the direction of the turn. Slow down before entering the turn, not during it.

questions.question: When riding in a group and taking a curve, what formation should you use?
questions.correctAnswerText: Single file.
questions.explanation: Groups normally ride staggered. Switch to single file when taking a curve, turning, entering a highway, or leaving a highway.

questions.question: Oil drippings and debris usually collect in which part of a lane?
questions.correctAnswerText: The center
questions.explanation: Oil drippings and debris from cars and trucks collect in the center of the lane.

questions.question: Where should you position your motorcycle when entering a curve?

options.text: On the outside of the curve
On the inside of the curve
Wherever traffic and road conditions require

questions.correctAnswerText: Wherever traffic and road conditions require
questions.explanation: Every curve is different. Choose a lane position based on conditions and adjust as needed.

questions.question: You see a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights ahead. What should you do?

options.text: Stop on the road behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait for the emergency vehicle to move.
Move to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle, tow truck, or roadside assistance vehicle with flashing lights, change lanes to give it space and slow down. Be ready to stop.

questions.question: The Motorcycle Safety Foundation teaches a "SEE" strategy for safe riding. What does "SEE" mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Search, Evaluate, and Execute.
questions.explanation: "SEE" stands for Search, Evaluate, and Execute. This is a strategy for making safe decisions while riding.

questions.question: Drivers can usually see a motorcycle best when it is in which lane position?
questions.correctAnswerText: The center
questions.explanation: The center lane position is usually best for following a car because it puts you in the driver's rearview mirror. Always be ready to change positions based on traffic and conditions.
